indicators.note: giving something a treatment works it over, so the letters of the two words are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from bugs that need treating for sepsis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges the ten letters of NEED SEPTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Many-legged arthropods scuttling about are a classic example of creepy-crawlies, alongside spiders and beetles.

clue.text: A bird in each hand is never- ending

indicators.note: the bird is placed in the abbreviation for each, enclosed by its two letters

parts.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price lists
a tern is a seabird
L stands for left, as in left hand

explanation.surface: A twist on the proverb about a bird in the hand, as if each hand held one forever.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb invites reading 'A bird in the hand' as a unit, but 'in' is the containment signal and 'hand' is just left, as in left hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without an end goes on for all time, the plain synonym for lasting forever.

indicators.note: the hat is worn around the daughter, so her letter sits inside the word for hat

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Mark's daughter is wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' reads as a man's name; it is the definition, a written mark. TILE is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy diacritic over the n in Spanish is a printed mark placed on a letter.

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a dial is a control knob

explanation.surface: A president managed to take control of the dinner arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to a meal, especially the main midday or evening meal.

clue.text: Checker on board liner shows drawing ability

parts.note: a checker on a board game is a draughtsman, a piece in draughts (the British name for checkers)
an ocean liner is a ship

explanation.surface: A checker aboard an ocean liner proves to be a fine draughtsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers, and its pieces are draughtsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill at technical or artistic sketching is the craft of the person who makes drawings.

clue.text: Belt worn by a Persian governor

indicators.note: a belt worn by something goes round it, so the belt's letters wrap around the a

parts.note: a strap is a belt

explanation.surface: A sash or belt worn by an ancient Persian official.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Persia a provincial ruler under the king held this title, a historical term for a governor.

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word pundit is taken

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A pundit's first verdict dismissed the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' reads as a critic's sneer but just means LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama staged in a theatre is a performance.

clue.text: One has aspirations before the bid

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a tender is a bid for a contract

explanation.surface: Someone harbours ambitions before submitting the bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant to a throne aspires to a position, so one with aspirations fits this person.

clue.text: A Tory peer is to give an explanation

parts.note: C stands for Conservative, the party of the Tories
a count is a nobleman, a peer

explanation.surface: A Conservative lord is called on to explain himself.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party; 'peer' looks like a fellow but means a noble.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to explain it, the verb sense of a report or reckoning.

definitions.meaning: to direct someone to do something, as in told to leave
William ..., the Swiss folk hero who shot an apple from his son's head

explanation.surface: Order an archer about.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to order someone; the other is the legendary Swiss bowman William of the apple story.

clue.text: He attracts constituents but only with difficulty

indicators.note: the words are treated as a set of component letters, to be recombined in a new order

explanation.surface: A politician wins over voters, though only with effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' suggests voters but signals rearranging HE ATTRACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: managed at a stretch means achieved by straining, with some difficulty.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to tend a patient is to nurse them

explanation.surface: A popular nurse receives a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Propose to' looks like marriage, but 'Propose' is the definition, meaning plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose doing something is to plan or mean to do it, a synonym.

clue.text: Obliged to pull back when about to consider force

indicators.note: the reversed pull goes about the other pieces, enclosing them
the word for pulling is turned back to front

parts.note: to lug is to pull or drag
to rate is to judge or consider
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: Someone thankful must pull back when about to weigh up a show of force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives GUL, and 'when about' wraps those letters around the rest; 'when' is part of the signal, not a time link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling obliged to someone means owing thanks, so the two are synonyms.

indicators.note: the jack takes the tirade straight after it, receiving it on its end

parts.note: a jack is a flag flown at a ship's bow, as in the Union Jack
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: Jack takes a shameless dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name; it is a ship's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagrant act is openly shameless, so it is a synonym for something bold and unashamed.

clue.text: Winger died in game on island

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the next
the letter for died is placed in the word for the game

parts.note: golf is a game
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
an inch is a small island in Scotland

explanation.surface: A football winger dies during a match played on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic way to describe any bird, which has wings; here a small finch with yellow wing bars.

definitions.meaning: deference owed, as in filial obligation to parents
a tax charged on imports, collected by customs

explanation.surface: Honour local traditions.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is moral obligation, the respect owed; the other is the import tax charged at customs.

parts.note: E is a musical key
the is the definite article
real feelings are sincere, heartfelt

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether a key article is sincere, dismissing it as insubstantial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airy and insubstantial seems not of the physical world, so it has no material form.

definitions.meaning: past tense of fall, to drop to the ground
a moorland hill in northern England, as in the Lake District

explanation.surface: Someone toppled down a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the past of fall; the other is the northern English word for a mountain or moor.

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sure means certain, guaranteed

explanation.surface: A removal firm promises an assured delivery time.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing out or deleting something is its removal, a synonym.

indicators.note: to make up is to compose, so the letters are composed afresh into a new order

explanation.surface: Maria is allowed to invent things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make up stuff' reads as lying, but 'stuff' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric or substance is stuff, the noun sense of matter or cloth.

parts.note: a band is a group, musical or otherwise

explanation.surface: A group of musicians goes on leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert someone or quit a place is to leave it behind, a synonym.

definitions.meaning: a shepherd's hooked staff, used to catch sheep

explanation.surface: Shepherds grab the livestock thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves are criminals; a shepherd's hooked staff is the other sense, held in the hand.

clue.text: Drug that can be helpful in conflict that's goin' on

parts.note: war is armed conflict
faring means going on, and the apostrophe drops the final g, giving farin'

explanation.surface: A medicine proves useful in a war that is still dragging on.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g in 'goin'' tells the solver to drop it from the synonym too.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticoagulant medicine that thins the blood, helpful against clots, though also used as rat poison.

clue.text: Make beloved's aim, to get attention

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A lover's aim is to get the beloved to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone's affection is to cause them to hold you dear.

clue.text: Material dug up is put back

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the word back means writing it in the reverse direction

parts.note: mined means dug up from the ground

explanation.surface: Material that was excavated is replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reads as reburial but reverses MINED.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough cotton twill used for jeans is a kind of fabric.

indicators.note: the name's letters are prepared, made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man named Ron Butcher mixes some paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark reddish-brown earth colour made by heating natural iron oxide is a pigment.

clue.text: Backing for some Macedonians is swelling

indicators.note: the letters taken are read backwards
only part of the word Macedonians is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Some Macedonians give their backing to something growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks EDON from Macedonians and 'Backing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump or knob on a body part, such as a lymph gland, is a swelling.

parts.note: set means arranged, as a table is set
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone booked a hotel for a man named Adamson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adamson' looks like a surname; it means a son of Adam, and the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve's third son was born after Cain and Abel.

parts.note: supple means flexible, agile
men are people

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word take is used

explanation.surface: Nimble folk start by taking a dietary additive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added to a diet or text, such as a vitamin pill, is an extra, an addition.
